records.episode_title: Remove an ineligible model from the generated built-in catalog
atomic_titles: Exclude an ineligible discovered model from the built-in catalog
Reconcile capability tests with catalog membership
workflow_titles: Remove an ineligible model from a generated built-in catalog
when_to_use: An upstream catalog still reports a model that product policy classifies as retired, redundant, or unsuitable for the built-in catalog.
The repository generates provider catalogs from upstream metadata and already has a provider-scoped exclusion boundary.
Tests or call sites currently treat the model as a built-in catalog member.
anti_goals: Do not edit generated catalog shards directly when the generator is the source of truth.
Do not remove the provider, change request routing, or alter capabilities of unrelated admitted models.
Do not suppress all models from the upstream provider when only one identifier is ineligible.
Do not retain capability assertions for a model whose required invariant is absence.
validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to prove the identifier was not excluded and was treated as a catalog member.
Inspect the generator path to prove upstream candidates pass through the provider-scoped exclusion predicate before serialization.
Assert the generated provider catalog does not contain the excluded identifier.
Assert retained built-in entries still have their expected routing and capability metadata.
Run the provider-specific regression test; run broader repository checks only when required by the repository's validation policy.
stop_conditions: Stop if the pinned change does not modify an implementation-bearing catalog boundary.
Stop if the target model is intended to remain selectable and only metadata needs correction.
Stop if no generated or runtime catalog call site can be traced from the changed filter.
Defer completion if catalog hydration or the provider-specific test cannot establish the absence invariant.

records.episode_title: Move curated model-picker metadata to a remotely refreshable catalog with resilient local fallbacks
atomic_titles: Define a versioned catalog for curated capability metadata
Reject incompatible catalog data before use
Resolve remote metadata through a bounded cache and fallback ladder
Adapt provider catalog entries to stable consumer shapes
Use dynamic curation without weakening picker invariants
workflow_titles: Externalize curated capability metadata without making selection depend on the network
when_to_use: Curated model or capability lists change more frequently than application releases.
Consumers already have bundled curated defaults that can serve as a safe last-resort snapshot.
Remote metadata can be separated from live capability, pricing, availability, or authorization data and reconciled at a defined selection boundary.
anti_goals: Do not make the remote catalog the sole source required for the picker to function.
Do not move volatile pricing, context limits, availability, authorization, or other live provider facts into a slowly cached curation manifest.
Do not bypass existing capability, pricing, tier, or availability filters merely because an identifier appears in the remote catalog.
Do not expose the generic manifest representation directly to consumers that already depend on stable provider-specific result shapes.
validation_ladder: Contract level: accept the supported manifest and reject incompatible versions and malformed provider/model entries.
Resolution level: prove persistence, fresh-cache reuse, forced refresh, and stale-cache recovery after network failure.
Adaptation level: prove stable provider-specific output shapes, disabled behavior, and override precedence.
Integration level: prove public helpers prefer remote curation and return bundled snapshots when the catalog is unavailable.
Consumer level: exercise model and authentication flows to confirm existing live capability, pricing, availability, and access checks remain authoritative.
stop_conditions: Stop if no bundled or otherwise trustworthy fallback exists and offline operation is required.
Stop if malformed or unsupported catalog data can reach selection consumers without rejection.
Stop if a fetch or cache failure can raise through the picker instead of producing a fallback result.
Stop if adopting remote identifiers removes or bypasses existing live eligibility checks.
Defer promotion as fully runtime-validated when the focused tests cannot be executed in the available environment.

records.episode_title: Refresh credential-scoped model metadata before starting turns
atomic_titles: Reconcile cached capability metadata with the active credentials
Reconcile capability metadata before constructing a turn
Revalidate wakeup ownership after asynchronous discovery
workflow_titles: Refresh identity-bound capability metadata before starting turns
when_to_use: Capability or model metadata is cached in memory and scoped, directly or indirectly, to an authenticated identity.
Credentials can rotate, be lazily resolved, or be shared across multiple turn-start paths while the process remains alive.
Turn construction consumes catalog fields such as context limits or request capability flags.
anti_goals: Do not make remote catalog discovery a mandatory condition for starting a turn.
Do not unconditionally fetch the catalog when static metadata is used or the resolved identity already matches the cached entry.
Do not refresh after the turn context has already captured capability metadata.
Do not let an interrupted queued-work wakeup resume merely because asynchronous discovery completed.
validation_ladder: Unit/integration-test lazy credential rotation to prove identity comparison uses newly resolved credentials rather than the previously cached identity.
Test successful refresh after another identity replaces the shared catalog; assert turn-visible limits and capability-derived request fields use the discovered metadata.
Test discovery failure and credential-resolution timeout; assert the turn starts within the deadline and uses existing bundled or cached fallback metadata.
Exercise every applicable trigger path, including direct user input and queued mailbox wakeups, and assert the request uses the active credential.
Add a focused cancellation or replacement race test for the post-discovery wakeup ownership check.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the catalog entry has no observable identity association and mismatch cannot be established safely.
Stop if no bounded fallback exists and adding best-effort discovery would silently weaken a required hard-failure contract.
Stop if an applicable turn-start path cannot be identified before capability metadata is captured.
Do not claim complete race validation until the interrupted-wakeup ownership branch has a dedicated test oracle.

records.episode_title: Register a model generation's token capabilities in authoritative and browser-safe catalogs
atomic_titles: Register specific input and output capabilities before family fallbacks
Synchronize the isolated consumer's capability mirror
workflow_titles: Update ordered model capabilities across authoritative and isolated catalogs
when_to_use: A recognized model generation is being classified by a broader family rule or a global default instead of its documented capabilities.
The repository has an ordered capability catalog and one or more isolated consumers that intentionally mirror it.
anti_goals: Do not change token-limit lookup, normalization, compaction, or request-clamping algorithms when correcting catalog metadata is sufficient.
Do not replace or widen the broad family fallback, because older or unknown family members must retain their established behavior.
Do not treat the provider's maximum configurable output as the default output value when the documented default is lower.
validation_ladder: Inspect rule ordering to confirm the specific identifier is tested before the broad family fallback in every input table.
Probe authoritative input and output lookup results for the target identifier.
Probe an existing family identifier to detect unintended fallback changes.
Run the same probes against each isolated mirror and compare results.
Add and run explicit regression tests for the new identifier in both modes; this final rung is deferred because commit 945cf3c8 added no such tests and the bundle contains no status-check evidence.
stop_conditions: Stop if the capability values are unverified or distinguish maximum configurable output from default output ambiguously.
Stop if normalization transforms the proposed identifier so the new rule cannot match as intended.
Stop if a required isolated consumer has different lookup semantics that cannot be reconciled by equivalent metadata entries.
Do not claim full automated validation until target-specific regression assertions or equivalent status-check evidence exist.

records.episode_title: Keep dynamically discovered provider error registries catchable
atomic_titles: Keep only catchable types in a dynamic error registry
workflow_titles: Repair a provider exception registry that admits non-catchable classes
when_to_use: A runtime error reports that a class in an except clause does not inherit from the language's exception base.
A provider module exposes ordinary classes whose names satisfy the adapter's error-name convention.
An adapter constructs a catch tuple by combining provider-module discovery with an explicit metadata registry.
anti_goals: Do not classify an export as an exception solely because its name ends with an error-like suffix.
Do not add retry metadata for an ordinary provider payload or event class merely to satisfy a discovery-list consistency check.
Do not change retry decisions, user-facing descriptions, or handling semantics for valid provider exceptions unless separate evidence requires it.
Do not normalize provider error message or payload contents; this episode concerns exception-type classification and catchability.
validation_ladder: Static diff check: confirm discovery combines the naming convention with a catchability/subclass predicate and the known invalid explicit entry is absent.
Registry check: instantiate the adapter and assert the emitted exception tuple is nonempty and every member is a BaseException subclass.
Focused regression check: assert the identified ordinary error-like export is not present in the emitted tuple.
Consumer check: raise a representative provider exception through a retry or reporting call site and verify normal metadata-driven handling occurs without TypeError.
Project check: run the focused exception and send-chat test modules in the pinned dependency environment.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the allegedly invalid provider export cannot be inspected or its inheritance relationship cannot be established.
Stop if consumers do not use the registry in language-level exception handling; this workflow would address the wrong boundary.
Do not claim complete validation if only registry construction is tested and no catch path or all-members-catchable assertion is available.
Stop and investigate separately if subclass inspection itself encounters non-class exports matching the name convention, because the pinned implementation assumes such matching exports are classes.

records.episode_title: Reject runtime wrapper instances as provider error bodies
atomic_titles: Accept only plain structured objects as error bodies
workflow_titles: Normalize ambiguous object-valued provider error payloads without losing diagnostics
when_to_use: A provider or transport SDK stores heterogeneous values in fields treated as error bodies.
Displayed errors contain serialized wrapper internals or stream state instead of the exception message.
Existing filtering recognizes only a specific runtime capability, such as a pipe method, and misses other class-based wrappers.
anti_goals: Do not remove support for string error bodies.
Do not suppress non-empty plain parsed JSON payloads merely because they are object-valued.
Do not redesign provider-specific call sites or error-message prefixes when the defect is in the shared payload-admission boundary.
Do not infer body legitimacy from serializability or enumerable keys alone.
validation_ladder: Unit-check a class-instance response body without a node-style pipe method: body must be absent and the diagnostic message must survive.
Unit-check a class instance in the alternate nested error slot: body must be absent and the diagnostic message must remain exact.
Compatibility-check a non-empty plain parsed object: it must still serialize into the normalized body.
Confirm downstream formatting selects the message when no body is admitted and selects status/body only for an admitted separate body.
Inspect all shared-normalizer call sites to verify the central guard covers affected adapters without provider-specific duplication.
stop_conditions: Stop if the failing value is a documented custom-prototype payload that must be surfaced; define a different admissibility contract before changing behavior.
Stop if no downstream path prefers the normalized body over the message, because the observed symptom then has another cause.
Stop if representative legitimate structured payloads cannot be distinguished from runtime wrappers with an evidence-backed invariant.

records.episode_title: Add bounded provider error details to failed API-call diagnostics
atomic_titles: Include available HTTP status in failure diagnostics
Show bounded details for bad-request failures
workflow_titles: Enrich provider failure diagnostics with bounded payload context
when_to_use: A shared provider-call boundary catches exceptions that carry HTTP status metadata not currently shown to the operator.
HTTP 400 exceptions may carry actionable response-body details that are absent from, or lost by cleaning, the ordinary exception message.
Streaming and non-streaming request paths converge on the same exception-diagnostic boundary.
anti_goals: Do not change retry, fallback, authentication refresh, context compression, interruption, or client-error classification policy.
Do not emit response bodies for every HTTP status.
Do not print an unbounded provider payload or replace the existing cleaned summary with the raw body.
Do not treat this diagnostic presentation change as full provider-payload schema normalization.
validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to verify that status and body were previously absent from visible diagnostics.
Inspect the pinned diff to verify conditional status annotation and the HTTP-400-only body branch.
Run `git diff --check` across the exact parent and pinned ref.
Add or execute focused output-capture tests for status present/absent and body short/long/empty/non-400 cases before treating the behavior as runtime-validated.
Exercise both streaming and non-streaming request paths because both feed the shared exception boundary.
stop_conditions: Stop if the exception type does not expose stable status or body metadata and no evidence-backed adapter is available.
Stop or redesign if response bodies can contain secrets and no acceptable redaction policy exists.
Do not claim completion from source inspection alone when automated runtime validation is required by the consuming project.
Stop if implementing the diagnostics would require changing recovery policy, because that is outside this workflow's grounded scope.

records.episode_title: Normalize byte-encoded API error response bodies as UTF-8 without altering unrecognized payloads
atomic_titles: Recognize byte-shaped error payloads without corrupting other data
Decode recognized error bytes as UTF-8 text
workflow_titles: Normalize byte-encoded provider errors before logging and propagation
when_to_use: A provider client sometimes exposes an error response body as a byte array or as comma-separated numeric bytes.
Multi-byte UTF-8 text is currently mojibake because byte values are converted directly to characters.
Normalization can run at a shared failure boundary before logging and propagation.
anti_goals: Do not rewrite ordinary textual or structured error payloads.
Do not accept fractional, negative, non-numeric, or greater-than-255 values as bytes.
Do not swallow, replace, or convert the original request rejection into success.
Do not redesign telemetry, retry behavior, authentication handling, or provider request routing.
validation_ladder: Unit-check admission and preservation boundaries with ordinary text, malformed serialized values, and out-of-range values.
Unit-check raw byte-array decoding with a known ASCII payload.
Unit-check serialized multi-byte UTF-8 decoding with both two-byte and three-byte characters.
Integration-check the request rejection boundary: normalization occurs before error logging and the original error object remains rejected/rethrown.
Separately verify every provider failure path that should share the contract, including stream creation and any errors raised during stream iteration.
stop_conditions: Stop if the response object or response-body field cannot be established from runtime evidence.
Stop and preserve the payload if serialized elements are not all integral bytes in the inclusive 0-255 range.
Defer decoding when the transport encoding is not known to be UTF-8.
Do not claim completion for failure paths that do not invoke the normalization boundary.

records.episode_title: Restore interactive terminal state before exiting on an uncaught exception
atomic_titles: Scope the uncaught-failure handler to the interactive lifecycle
Finalize a live terminal before fatal exit
workflow_titles: Restore an interactive terminal on an uncaught process failure
when_to_use: A long-running interactive process enables raw input, hides the cursor, or enables terminal protocols that ordinary process termination will not reliably restore.
Asynchronous callbacks or extension code can throw outside local try/catch boundaries while the terminal remains connected.
anti_goals: Do not convert uncaught failures into continued execution after potentially inconsistent process state.
Do not run normal terminal writes when the terminal is already known to be dead or disconnected.
Do not replace graceful shutdown or signal-specific cleanup paths with the last-resort crash path.
validation_ladder: Static diff validation: confirm the first-parent change adds only the crash finalizer and lifecycle-managed listener without whitespace errors.
Lifecycle validation: confirm initialization installs the listener before UI start and normal cleanup removes it.
Resource-contract validation: confirm the invoked UI stop operation restores the cursor and delegates to terminal cleanup that disables protocols and restores raw mode.
Deferred behavioral validation: trigger an uncaught asynchronous throw under a pseudo-terminal and assert nonzero exit plus restored terminal settings and cursor state.
stop_conditions: Stop if no reliable process-level uncaught-failure interception point exists.
Stop if the available cleanup primitive writes to a terminal that may already be dead; use the established dead-terminal emergency path instead.
Stop if listener removal cannot be tied to the interactive component's normal lifecycle.
Do not claim behavioral regression coverage until a pseudo-terminal test or equivalent runtime oracle is present.

records.episode_title: Isolate stdio child-process diagnostics from the interactive terminal
atomic_titles: Provision a reusable file-descriptor-backed diagnostic sink
Mark each child launch in the shared diagnostic stream
Bind child stderr to the selected diagnostic sink
workflow_titles: Isolate subprocess diagnostics from an interactive terminal UI
when_to_use: A library-managed child process defaults stderr to the parent process's terminal.
The parent concurrently renders an interactive terminal interface whose state can be corrupted by unsolicited writes.
Child stderr is diagnostic output rather than the protocol stream used for parent-child communication.
anti_goals: Do not redirect or modify the child's protocol-bearing stdin or stdout streams.
Do not redesign PID tracking, session initialization, reconnection, cancellation, or shutdown behavior.
Do not add a per-line pipe and reader thread solely to prefix diagnostics when a launch marker is sufficient.
Do not make failure to open an optional diagnostic log prevent the child from starting.
validation_ladder: Static boundary check: verify each affected spawn supplies an explicit stderr/errlog destination instead of relying on the library default.
Sink contract check: verify the preferred destination is append-mode, promptly flushed or line-buffered, reusable, and exposes the OS-level descriptor required by subprocess machinery.
Fallback check: force preferred-log creation failure and confirm startup can proceed through the null-device path; document the final parent-stderr degradation if even that open fails.
Lifecycle regression check: start the mocked stdio connection, initialize and discover tools, then shut it down successfully.
End-to-end isolation check: spawn a real child that writes a recognizable stderr payload and assert it appears in the diagnostic log but not in the terminal capture.
stop_conditions: Stop and redesign if stderr carries required protocol messages rather than diagnostics.
Stop if the subprocess library cannot attach the chosen sink directly or the sink lacks the required OS-level descriptor.
Do not claim complete terminal isolation when sink acquisition reaches the final parent-stderr fallback.
Do not claim automated regression coverage until a test directly asserts routing and terminal non-leakage.

records.episode_title: Interrupt non-TTY subprocesses without bypassing normal lifecycle completion
atomic_titles: Recognize only the interrupt control payload on closed non-TTY stdin
Propagate an interrupt without consuming lifecycle ownership
Drain interrupted-process output and preserve its real exit result
workflow_titles: Add lifecycle-safe interruption for a non-TTY subprocess
when_to_use: A long-running process is managed as a persistent session but was launched without a TTY or writable stdin.
The existing control surface represents Ctrl-C as an exact control-character payload.
Graceful interruption must run process signal handlers and preserve normal output and exit observation across local or remote execution.
anti_goals: Do not enable arbitrary stdin writes for processes whose stdin is closed.
Do not replace interrupt with hard termination or abort lifecycle observers immediately after signaling.
Do not fabricate a Ctrl-C exit code when the process can report its own handler-selected exit code.
Do not silently claim interrupt support on a backend that cannot implement it.
Do not redesign unrelated process start, read, termination, or hard-kill semantics.
validation_ladder: Unit/contract level: confirm the process abstraction accepts the typed interrupt operation while ordinary non-TTY input remains rejected.
Backend integration level: run a non-TTY process with a SIGINT trap through both local and remote execution; require trap output, its chosen exit code, and closed state.
End-to-end lifecycle level: send exact U+0003 through the session-control tool; require drained trap output, authentic exit metadata, and removal of the completed session.
Default-signal level: interrupt a process without a handler and require conventional Unix exit code 130.
Capability boundary: on an unsupported backend, require a model-visible unsupported-interrupt error and no fabricated success.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the session cannot distinguish the exact interrupt sentinel from ordinary input.
Stop and report unsupported if the backend cannot deliver the requested signal; do not fall back silently to hard-kill.
Stop and treat the implementation as incomplete if signaling consumes the process controller or aborts output/wait observers before final state is collected.
Stop and treat validation as failed if handler output, handler-selected exit status, default signal status, or session cleanup is lost.

records.episode_title: Synchronize native PTY exit with public lifecycle completion and make finalization resilient
atomic_titles: Reconcile native process exit with PTY lifecycle completion
Neutralize deferred resize work after process exit
Keep output failures from blocking process finalization
workflow_titles: Make PTY termination deterministic across asynchronous exit and output paths
when_to_use: A PTY-backed subprocess can terminate at the operating-system layer without reliably producing the library's public exit event.
Control operations may be queued internally and execute after process termination.
Output or lifecycle event consumers are outside the lifecycle owner's trust boundary and may throw during output processing or shutdown.
anti_goals: Do not immediately finalize at the native exit signal when a short bounded window is needed to drain trailing PTY output.

Do not suppress arbitrary resize, rendering, or consumer errors indiscriminately; contain only errors whose failure must not block lifecycle completion, and preserve logging or rethrow unrelated control errors.
Do not create separate cleanup implementations for native and public exit signals.
Do not change command semantics, output formatting, or successful interactive behavior beyond lifecycle hardening.
validation_ladder: Unit-test the post-exit control-operation guard by flushing a previously deferred resize after native termination.
Unit-test ordinary public-exit finalization with a throwing output consumer and a bounded completion timeout.
Unit-test the missing-public-exit scenario using the native exit signal, the complete drain interval, result metadata, and active-resource state.
Confirm both native and public exit signals converge on one idempotent finalizer so duplicate completion and cleanup are prevented.
stop_conditions: Stop if there is no trustworthy native termination signal or exit state to reconcile with the public lifecycle.
Stop if no bounded drain policy can be justified; an unbounded wait recreates the hang, while immediate cleanup may discard output.
Stop if the proposed interception requires swallowing unrelated operational errors or bypassing the normal shared cleanup path.
Stop and defer promotion if the regression tests cannot establish result resolution and resource-state cleanup.

records.episode_title: Resolve read-only path patterns against the repository root
atomic_titles: Align relative pattern discovery with the authoritative resource root
workflow_titles: Keep policy-scoped file selection stable across working-directory changes
when_to_use: A command accepts relative paths or glob patterns for policy-scoped resources and fails or resolves inconsistently after the process changes into a nested directory.
Path discovery and later canonicalization use different implicit bases, allowing ambient working-directory state to affect which resource receives the policy.
anti_goals: Do not broaden editable access or convert read-only resources into editable resources.
Do not restrict already-supported absolute or user-home-expanded resource paths.
Do not change repository membership rules, file contents, or the process current working directory as the repair.
validation_ladder: Inspect the implementation boundary and confirm relative discovery and downstream canonicalization use the same authoritative root.
Run the focused nested-working-directory test and confirm the canonical file is added to the read-only collection.
Exercise removal with the same root-relative name and confirm the canonical file leaves the collection.
Run the existing absolute external-file read-only test to detect accidental narrowing of accepted path forms.
Run the broader command test suite when its dependencies are available.
Run a patch-integrity check such as git diff --check.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the intended base for relative paths cannot be established from command semantics or call sites.
Stop if aligning the base would eliminate required absolute-path support or alter editable-access policy.
Do not claim runtime validation success when the test environment cannot collect the focused test.

records.episode_title: Harden dangerous-command approval boundaries and preserve explicit bypass semantics
atomic_titles: Capture process-wide bypass configuration at initialization
Require an exact machine decision token
Detect path-qualified and argument-bearing remote shell pipelines
Audit unattended dangerous-command auto-approvals
Exercise bypass behavior through the captured policy state
workflow_titles: Harden approval bypasses and unattended permission decisions
when_to_use: A permission or approval subsystem rereads mutable process state when deciding whether to bypass checks.
An external or model-generated response is parsed into an allow/deny decision using substring or otherwise permissive matching.
Equivalent dangerous command spellings evade a syntax-based classifier.
An unattended compatibility path intentionally auto-approves detected dangerous operations but does so silently.
anti_goals: Do not move bypass checks ahead of unconditional catastrophic-command or credential guards.
Do not remove session-scoped bypass controls or convert them into process-global state.
Do not change legacy unattended auto-approval into blocking behavior as part of an audit-only hardening change.
Do not treat arbitrary explanatory model text as an authoritative permission decision.
Do not broaden command patterns without retaining benign control cases to detect false positives.
validation_ladder: Inspect the parent/after diff to verify that both approval entry points share the captured bypass state and that unconditional guards still precede it.
Unit-test exact decision-token acceptance and conservative handling of all non-exact or failed responses.
Table-test newly supported dangerous syntax variants together with benign controls.
Capture warnings for the unattended dangerous-command branch and verify its legacy return value is unchanged.
Run direct-guard and consolidated-guard bypass tests, then run the broader approval test suite.
stop_conditions: Stop if lifecycle analysis cannot establish when trusted configuration is initialized relative to untrusted code execution.
Stop if changing bypass-state lifetime would break an authenticated runtime policy control rather than closing an unintended mutation path.
Stop if a broadened dangerous-command pattern produces unresolved benign false positives.
Stop if unattended behavior is not an intentional compatibility contract and requires a separate product decision about blocking.
Do not claim runtime validation complete when the required pinned checkout and test interpreter cannot be materialized.

records.episode_title: Align approval and patch-safety decisions with the effective split filesystem policy
atomic_titles: Classify execution approval from effective filesystem access
Propagate effective filesystem policy through every execution path
Delegate patch authorization to the shared effective-access query
Verify legacy configuration converts without permission drift
workflow_titles: Align permission decisions with effective filesystem access
when_to_use: A system has introduced a richer or split filesystem permission model but approval or safety consumers still inspect a legacy projection.
Different execution paths can reach the same approval decision with inconsistent policy inputs.
Local authorization code duplicates effective-access precedence or carveout calculations.
anti_goals: Do not introduce or redesign platform sandbox backend enforcement.
Do not change network-policy behavior except to verify legacy conversion equivalence.
Do not remove the legacy compatibility policy while call sites still require it for unrelated behavior.
Do not broaden filesystem access or suppress prompts merely to simplify the migration.
validation_ladder: Compile the affected request and context structures so every approval path must provide an effective filesystem policy.
Run focused unit tests for restricted versus external default approval requirements and Reject-mode behavior.
Run the contradictory-policy unmatched-command test to prove the split policy, not the legacy projection, controls escalation prompting.
Run intercepted-execution tests to cover wrapper parsing and policy fallback with the propagated context.
Run legacy configuration conversion and round-trip regression tests across unrestricted, read-only, and workspace-write cases.
Run existing patch-safety tests against writable, denied, unreadable, and unrestricted targets.
Run the broader codex-core test suite and test-target clippy after focused tests pass.
stop_conditions: Stop if no authoritative effective filesystem policy can be identified.
Stop if a consumer requires semantics not represented by the effective policy; extend the policy contract before replacing its logic.
Stop and defer platform-specific enforcement failures to the backend work responsible for that platform.
Do not declare validation complete if only test source or commit-listed commands are available without execution results.

records.episode_title: Route shell substitution through reviewable permission decisions with visible warnings
atomic_titles: Make implicit shell risks reviewable without weakening explicit denials
Detect shell substitution before lossy normalization and across the full syntax tree
Attach a shared risk warning to shell execution confirmations
Render execution warnings without hiding approval controls
workflow_titles: Replace inconsistent syntax denial with informed, policy-preserving review
when_to_use: A shell-like tool has syntactic-risk checks duplicated across permission layers or sibling tools and equivalent commands receive different decisions depending on unrelated rules.
A permission fix that removes a hard deny could expose read-only-classification blind spots or lossy-normalization bypasses.
The approval surface needs to explain a risk while retaining usable controls in constrained layouts.
anti_goals: Do not weaken or override explicit user-configured deny rules.
Do not classify substitution-bearing commands as read-only merely to make them executable.
Do not apply the agent-tool approval policy to separately scoped user-authored shell-injection defenses.
Do not make warnings themselves errors or force ask when an explicit allow rule intentionally grants permission.
validation_ladder: Unit-test the shared raw/stripped detection and warning helper with positive and negative commands.
Test primary AST and fallback classification for assignments, redirects, wrappers, and every supported substitution syntax.
Test permission decisions for standalone input, compound commands with unrelated matching rules, sibling tools, read-only controls, and explicit deny precedence.
Test confirmation producers for warning presence and absence.
Render interactive confirmations under ordinary, narrow, and compact height constraints and verify both warning and choices.
Run the affected multi-package regression suite and strict TypeScript build.
stop_conditions: Stop if explicit deny precedence is lost or an implicit-risk command becomes allow through any primary or fallback path.
Stop if raw and normalized detection disagree without a documented, tested reason.
Stop if a confirmation consumer cannot represent the warning without hiding or removing user choices.
Defer surfaces governed by a different threat model instead of applying the agent-tool policy indiscriminately.

records.episode_title: Keep absolute-path conversion usable when canonical resolution encounters a symlink loop
atomic_titles: Fall back to a lexical absolute path when canonical resolution fails
workflow_titles: Make absolute-path normalization resilient to symlink-resolution failures
when_to_use: A shared helper currently relies on canonical path resolution and a reproducible circular symbolic-link input causes that boundary to raise.
Downstream consumers require an absolute path, but do not require the fallback result to dereference every symlink.
anti_goals: Do not replace canonical resolution on the successful path.
Do not claim that the fallback identifies the physical filesystem target or validates path existence.
Do not broaden the change to unrelated repository-root discovery or path-containment behavior.
Do not suppress exceptions outside the explicitly selected resolution-failure classes.
validation_ladder: Reproduce that canonical resolution of a circular symlink raises at the normalization boundary.
Run the focused regression oracle that creates a circular symlink, calls the helper, and checks that the result is absolute.
Inspect unchanged callers to confirm they continue to use the hardened shared boundary for coder paths, repository paths, working-tree roots, and common-root conversion.
Run the broader path and repository test suites when the project's test dependencies are available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the failure cannot be reproduced at the shared normalization boundary.
Stop if affected callers require canonical or dereferenced identity rather than merely an absolute path.
Stop if the proposed fallback could be used for a security-sensitive containment decision without separate validation.
Defer completion if the focused regression test cannot be run in an environment with the project's test dependencies.

stop_conditions: Stop if installed records do not expose persisted source metadata; do not invent source identity from names or paths.
Stop if source identity is ambiguous across installed records until a disambiguation contract is established.
Stop and fail safely if neither canonical name nor recorded source matches the request.
Stop extraction-level validation claims short of asserting a successful local test run, because only the committed test oracle—not an execution result—was available in this checkout.

records.episode_title: Detect extension changes and reconcile the live runtime without restarting the session
atomic_titles: Classify extension file changes by safe refresh scope
Coordinate reload state and suppress self-generated watcher events
Refresh content capabilities in place
Rebuild the extension runtime from one coherent snapshot
Reload configured hooks without discarding session hooks
workflow_titles: Reconcile live extension changes at the narrowest safe scope
when_to_use: A long-lived process loads extensible capabilities from files that users or development tools can edit outside the process.
Some extension changes can be refreshed locally, while manifests, hooks, topology, or referenced configuration require a coherent whole-package rebuild.
Programmatic extension mutations and filesystem notifications may overlap or echo one another.
anti_goals: Do not hot-apply arbitrary or unknown extension files.
Do not treat security-sensitive hook edits as content-only refreshes.
Do not change extension discovery, installation-source, marketplace, or conversion semantics as part of reload coordination.
Do not follow extension-provided symlinks into arbitrary external paths.
Do not hide MCP, LSP, hook, or aggregated content-refresh failures behind a success message.
validation_ladder: Unit-test path classification for installed roots, linked roots, tracked referenced files, ignored files, topology creation/removal, and missing manifests.
Unit-test refresh state for deduplication, overlapping mutation suppression, changes during reload, stale-over-content priority, and failure retryability.
Unit-test content refresh for cache and command coverage, independent-leg settlement, aggregated errors, safe-mode behavior, debounce, and cancellation.
Unit-test configured-hook reload for session-hook preservation, enabled-state preservation, and transactional rollback.
Unit-test package runtime reconciliation for MCP-first behavior, LSP and hook failure propagation, best-effort legs, command rebuilding, and summary counts.

Exercise the interactive session by editing each supported file class and confirming either immediate capability visibility or a package-reload prompt, followed by successful reload or actionable failure feedback.
stop_conditions: Stop automatic refresh when the session enters safe or bare mode.
Stop content-only reconciliation and require package reload when package-stale state is set.
Stop classifying unknown files as reloadable unless a semantic owner and validation oracle are added.
Stop and retain retry-needed state when a material package reload leg fails.
Stop repeated automatic passes at the configured bound and surface the noisy-change failure.

records.episode_title: Close active terminal hyperlinks at truncation boundaries
atomic_titles: Close an active hyperlink before truncated output ends
workflow_titles: Repair hyperlink state when truncating terminal text
when_to_use: A text truncation or clipping function preserves embedded hyperlink control sequences in its retained prefix.
The original hyperlink closer can fall in the discarded suffix, leaving the retained output structurally unbalanced.
anti_goals: Do not remove hyperlink targets or visible label content that fits within the existing width budget.
Do not alter visible-width calculation, truncation position, padding, or ellipsis policy.
Do not treat a generic style reset as sufficient to close a separate hyperlink protocol.
validation_ladder: Inspect the before/after finalization diff to confirm the repair is limited to structured hyperlink closure.
Run the focused exact-output regression for a link whose closer is discarded by truncation.
Run the surrounding truncation tests covering width limits, styling resets, empty ellipses, wide graphemes, padding, and malformed escape prefixes.
Add or run an equivalent exact-output case for the alternate ST terminator before claiming both terminators have direct test coverage.
stop_conditions: Stop if the retained prefix is not available for state inspection.
Stop if terminal sequences cannot be parsed reliably enough to distinguish link opens from closes.
Defer completion if the fix changes the visible-width or truncation-selection contract without corresponding evidence and tests.
Do not claim runtime validation when the package test command cannot execute.

records.episode_title: Add a persistent policy for handing clicked links to the system browser
atomic_titles: Maintain a synchronized device-local link handoff preference
Expose the link handoff policy as a localized settings control
Apply the handoff policy at the central clicked-link boundary
workflow_titles: Add a user-selectable browser handoff policy for clicked links
when_to_use: A desktop or embedded application centrally intercepts link clicks and users need a persistent choice between an internal browser surface and the operating-system browser.
The application already has distinct internal-preview and external-handoff primitives that can remain authoritative for explicit actions.
anti_goals: Do not change the default destination for users who have not enabled the preference.
Do not replace or remove existing modifier, middle-click, authorization, special-surface, or non-web-scheme routing rules.
Do not make explicit Open in in-app browser or Open in external browser commands obey the ordinary-click preference.
Do not synchronize this device-specific UI preference through remote agent configuration.
validation_ladder: Store-level: verify default value, durable true/false writes, and cross-window event reconciliation.
Dispatcher-level: verify enabled ordinary clicks call the external bridge and create no internal preview.
Regression-level: verify disabled ordinary clicks still open internally and modifier clicks still open externally.
Override-level: verify explicit context-menu destinations remain available and the in-app action still opens a preview.
Integration-level: run the desktop typecheck and Vitest UI suite declared by the pinned package.
stop_conditions: Stop if there is no single application-owned boundary through which ordinary clicks can consistently enforce the policy.
Stop if external handoff cannot be distinguished from internal preview in a behavioral oracle.
Stop if adding the preference would override mandatory protocol or security routing.
Stop if the prior default and explicit destination commands cannot be preserved and tested.

records.episode_title: Route macOS workspace launches through an encoded application deep link
atomic_titles: Encode the requested target in an application-owned deep link
Hand the application-owned link to the operating-system launcher
workflow_titles: Replace an unreliable document-open handoff with an explicit application route
when_to_use: The operating-system launcher successfully selects or focuses the destination application but its generic document-open argument is not reliably honored.
The destination application provides a supported deep-link route capable of representing the requested target.
The target must survive transport through URL syntax without spaces, fragment markers, or other reserved characters changing its meaning.
anti_goals: Do not redesign application discovery, installation, architecture detection, or download behavior.
Do not shell-escape or concatenate the workspace into a URL manually when a structured query serializer is available.
Do not change the CLI workspace argument contract or optimize unrelated installer behavior.
Do not treat successful process launch alone as proof that the target was encoded or delivered correctly.
validation_ladder: Unit-test structured URL construction by parsing the result and asserting scheme, authority, route, and decoded query pairs.
Use a target containing URL-reserved characters to prove query serialization preserves target identity.
Inspect or spy on the operating-system command invocation to prove the encoded link, not the raw path, is handed off.
Exercise both the already-installed and install-then-launch call paths because both must converge on the corrected handoff.
On a supported platform with the desktop application available, run an end-to-end CLI launch and confirm the requested workspace is opened, not merely that the application is focused.
stop_conditions: Stop if the receiving application does not document or support an explicit route for the requested target.
Stop if URL parsing or query decoding does not reproduce the intended target.
Stop if any launch branch bypasses the corrected handoff boundary.
Stop if process success cannot be distinguished from successful target delivery; retain end-to-end validation as unresolved rather than claiming it.

records.episode_title: Replace repeated automatic browser launches with an explicit documentation handoff
atomic_titles: Replace automatic navigation with an explicit user-controlled handoff
Encode a deterministic empty-state handoff contract
workflow_titles: Make repeated empty-state documentation handoffs user-controlled
when_to_use: A command, status view, refresh path, or similarly repeatable interaction automatically opens documentation when no resources are configured.
Multiple callers converge on the same empty-state branch, making an otherwise helpful browser handoff repeatable.
The external documentation target should remain available, but navigation should require deliberate user action.
anti_goals: Do not remove or silently change the established documentation target.
Do not alter configured-resource status, discovery, authentication, or refresh behavior beyond the shared empty-state return path.
Do not optimize browser-launch mechanics or add another environment-specific automatic-launch policy.
Do not claim that the external URL destination or the internal documentation command itself was exercised unless separately validated.
validation_ladder: Diff-level check: confirm removal of the external opener dependency, environment branch, and invocation while retaining the same documentation URL.
Call-site check: confirm default, list, and refresh status paths all converge on the repaired empty-state behavior.
Unit-contract check: produce the empty state and assert the exact informational response containing both the external URL and internal documentation route.
Broader regression check, when the checkout is runnable: execute the command test file and verify configured-resource status tests remain successful.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the empty-state predicate or its browser-launch side effect cannot be established from before-state code.
Stop if removing navigation would violate an explicit requirement that this interaction launch a browser.
Stop if preserving the link target or another actionable handoff is impossible.
Do not claim end-to-end link integrity or successful internal documentation routing without a separate oracle for those destinations.

records.episode_title: Extend package installation and validation through Python 3.14 across Linux and Windows
atomic_titles: Align package metadata with the expanded runtime range
Partition dependency constraints by runtime capability
Preserve runtime markers in generated release requirements
Expand cross-platform validation to every supported runtime
workflow_titles: Extend a packaged application across new interpreter releases
when_to_use: Package metadata must admit one or more new interpreter releases.
At least one dependency or removed standard-library module requires different treatment across old and new interpreter cohorts.
The repository commits generated dependency artifacts and validates installation on multiple operating systems.
anti_goals: Do not drop an older supported interpreter merely to use one unconditional modern dependency pin.
Do not claim runtime support solely by changing package classifiers or the interpreter upper bound.
Do not let a lock generated on one host replace cross-runtime marker branches with host-specific pins.
Do not broaden unrelated application behavior or optimize dependency versions beyond what compatibility requires.
validation_ladder: Statically verify that metadata bounds and classifiers agree on Python 3.10-3.14.
Regenerate dependency artifacts and verify that compatibility-sensitive packages retain mutually exclusive runtime markers without unconditional conflicting pins.
Install the source package and run pytest for every supported interpreter on Linux and Windows.
Install the published package for every supported interpreter on Linux and Windows and compare its reported version with the latest release tag.
Require observed CI status results before treating configured workflow coverage as proven execution success.
stop_conditions: Stop if any newly admitted interpreter has no viable dependency set or required compatibility backport.
Stop if generated artifacts cannot preserve the runtime-specific policy without conflicting assignments.
Stop promotion if either operating-system family lacks source-install/test coverage for a claimed supported runtime.
Defer success claims when CI execution or release-install results are unavailable.

records.episode_title: Add an architecture-specific Windows release artifact across build, packaging, and publication
atomic_titles: Extend the release target contract and prerequisites
Package the correct native payload for each architecture
Publish the new artifact in every release path
workflow_titles: Add a new architecture to a cross-platform binary release
when_to_use: A supported operating-system family lacks a release artifact for one hardware architecture.
The binary includes optional or external native components whose packaged payload must match the target architecture.
Release publication enumerates artifact filenames explicitly.
anti_goals: Do not embed every platform's native modules into every compiled binary.
Do not change archive conventions for already-supported operating-system families without a separate requirement.
Do not treat artifact generation alone as completion when release upload lists are explicit.
Do not claim runtime compatibility from archive extraction alone.
validation_ladder: Static contract check: the target, dependencies, staging directory, compiler target, native-module mapping, archive name, and publication name agree.
Build check: the full default target matrix completes the new target using the required compiler version.
Package check: the archive contains the family-specific executable and architecture-specific native payload.
Structural check: delete the staging directory and successfully extract the produced archive.
Publication check: verify the release exposes the expected artifact after either creation or fallback upload.
Runtime check, deferred in this episode: execute the artifact on the target architecture and exercise functionality that loads the packaged native module.
stop_conditions: Stop if the compiler does not support the target at the pinned toolchain version and no reviewed upgrade is available.
Stop if required architecture-specific dependencies or native modules cannot be resolved.
Stop if the produced artifact name differs from the name consumed by release publication.
Do not declare complete runtime support when only static inspection or archive extraction has been observed.

records.episode_title: Restore the desktop packaging toolchain in isolated installer stages and report missing prerequisites as failure
atomic_titles: Restore the packaging toolchain inside an isolated stage
Fail requested packaging when its toolchain remains unavailable
workflow_titles: Make an isolated packaging stage restore prerequisites and report truthful completion
when_to_use: Installer stages run in separate processes or otherwise do not inherit PATH mutations from prerequisite stages.
A packaging stage depends on a runtime that may have been installed into an application-managed directory.
The current behavior can skip a requested build and still report successful completion.
anti_goals: Do not make optional command-line or first-launch flows rebuild the desktop application when they did not request packaging.
Do not treat signing, notarization, or distributable image production as part of this prerequisite-restoration fix.
Do not accept process success alone when the expected packaged artifact is absent.
Do not replace the managed toolchain policy with an unrelated packaging system.
validation_ladder: Run Bash syntax validation and patch whitespace validation.
Exercise prerequisite reconciliation with the managed runtime installed but omitted from the initial PATH.
Exercise the negative path with the required executable still unavailable and assert nonzero exit plus an ok:false stage result.
Exercise the positive packaging path and assert that one of the supported application artifact paths exists.
Perform an end-to-end installer launch check using the produced application artifact on each supported packaging architecture.
stop_conditions: Stop and report failure if prerequisite reconciliation cannot expose the required executable.
Stop and report failure if dependency installation or the package build command returns nonzero.
Stop and report failure if the build command completes but no recognized artifact is found.
Defer promotion beyond a candidate workflow until automated shell-stage coverage or equivalent repeatable validation is available.

records.episode_title: Publish the prebuilt CLI bundle with platform-specific optional dependencies
atomic_titles: Require and stage the generated release bundle
Reconcile the package manifest with a bundled runtime
Gate bundled preparation by publication target
workflow_titles: Package a prebuilt CLI without losing platform-specific runtime support
when_to_use: A release pipeline already generates a bundled executable, but the package manifest and files allowlist still describe source-oriented or separately compiled output.
The package needs optional native dependencies selected by operating system or architecture even though ordinary runtime dependencies are absorbed into the bundle.
Different publication targets require distinct package preparation behavior.
anti_goals: Do not redesign the bundler or change the runtime behavior of the generated executable.
Do not remove platform-specific optional dependencies merely because ordinary dependencies are bundled.
Do not apply the bundled manifest transformation to registry paths with a separate packaging contract.
Do not treat successful bundle generation alone as proof that the final package tarball is complete.
validation_ladder: Precondition: verify the generated bundle directory exists and contains the expected executable before mutating the package.
Filesystem: verify the previous package-local bundle is replaced by the generated artifact tree.
Manifest: verify files and bin resolve to the staged bundle; verify bundled-away fields are absent; compare optional dependencies with the authoritative root set after exclusions.
Pipeline: verify the transformation is conditionally ordered after bundle generation and before CLI publication.

Package: execute the existing npm publication dry-run for the eligible registry path and inspect the packed artifact; this is recommended by the workflow contract but no successful run is present in the supplied evidence.

Regression: add isolated tests for missing-bundle failure, stale-destination replacement, manifest rewriting, optional-dependency filtering, and registry gating; these tests are deferred because the pinned change added none.
stop_conditions: Stop before manifest mutation and publication if the generated bundle is missing.
Stop if the expected bundled executable is absent after staging.
Stop if the transformed manifest still points outside the published files allowlist.
Stop if required platform-specific optional dependencies are lost or development-only exclusions remain.
Do not apply this workflow to a publication target whose packaging contract requires the original manifest layout.

records.episode_title: Redact secrets at terminal exception-result and ACP stderr boundaries
atomic_titles: Redact exception diagnostics before returning them to the caller
Install redaction on an independently configured diagnostic log sink
workflow_titles: Close secret leaks at structured-result and log-output boundaries
when_to_use: A structured error result exposes raw exception messages, tracebacks, command context, or comparable diagnostic text to an external consumer.
A subsystem replaces inherited logging handlers or formatters and therefore bypasses an established application-wide redaction formatter.
An existing, tested sensitive-text redaction policy can be reused at the emission boundary.
anti_goals: Do not remove the error result, traceback field, log destination, log layout, filters, or status information merely to avoid leakage.
Do not redesign or broaden the secret-detection algorithm when the demonstrated defect is an emission boundary that fails to invoke the existing policy.
Do not claim closure of unrelated secret-emission gaps outside the inspected exception-result and ACP stderr surfaces.
validation_ladder: Static comparison: confirm each raw emission point in the parent is replaced by the shared redaction function or formatter without changing unrelated routing and response structure.
Branch-level structured-result tests: inject a secret-bearing generic exception and a degraded-fail connection exception, then inspect every returned diagnostic field.
Sink-level logging test: format a secret-bearing record through the exact handler installed by subsystem logging setup.
Integration check: run the three focused regression tests together in an environment with the repository's test dependencies.
Broader regression check: run the surrounding terminal-tool, ACP-adapter, and redaction test suites to detect formatting, filtering, or response-contract regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if the parent and after states do not identify a concrete unredacted emission boundary.
Stop if redaction is applied only to an internal logger copy while another consumer-facing copy remains raw.
Stop if the focused tests do not assert both secret absence and preservation of the required diagnostic contract.
Do not report runtime validation as passed when the test runner or dependencies are unavailable.

records.episode_title: Remove sensitive response metadata and tool arguments from informational diagnostics
atomic_titles: Omit response metadata from successful connection diagnostics
Omit tool arguments from invocation diagnostics
workflow_titles: Remove sensitive values from routine diagnostics while preserving operational context
when_to_use: An info-level success or invocation message serializes a complete metadata collection or request/tool argument payload.
The sensitive value is needed by runtime processing but is not required to identify the diagnostic event.
The diagnostic can remain useful with bounded identifiers such as a connection target, correlation ID, or operation name.
anti_goals: Do not disable successful-connection or tool-invocation diagnostics entirely.
Do not remove metadata or payloads from protocol processing, persistence, or tool execution.
Do not broaden the change to error diagnostics, payload storage, or unrelated telemetry without separate evidence and validation.
Do not optimize diagnostic verbosity or performance beyond eliminating the sensitive formatting operations.
validation_ladder: Inspect the parent state to identify the exact metadata and payload expressions copied into routine logs.
Inspect the implementation diff to confirm only the sensitive formatting and now-unused import or local value were removed.
Verify the remaining messages retain the intended connection, correlation, and operation identifiers.
Trace downstream code to confirm response metadata is still consumed for protocol behavior and the original tool call is still persisted and executed.
Run focused log-capture tests with sentinel header and tool-argument values when such a harness is available; assert sentinels are absent and retained identifiers are present.
Run the affected transport and core test suites or compile checks to detect behavioral or unused-import regressions.
stop_conditions: Stop if the before-state diagnostic cannot be established from source or captured output.
Stop if removing the formatted value also changes connection negotiation, response metadata interpretation, persistence, or tool execution.
Stop and separate the work if additional diagnostic boundaries have different sensitivity contracts or validation oracles.
Do not claim runtime log-redaction coverage until a log-capture test or equivalent execution oracle has been run.

records.episode_title: Honor the telemetry payload-consent flag across diagnostic logging paths
atomic_titles: Gate diagnostic payload fields on explicit logging consent
Reduce mixed diagnostic metadata to explicitly safe aggregates
Apply the same payload boundary across telemetry sinks
workflow_titles: Enforce consent-aware redaction at diagnostic emission boundaries
when_to_use: A runtime privacy or consent flag is intended to control prompt, response, command, policy, rationale, or comparable free-form diagnostic payloads.
The same logical event is serialized through multiple record types or telemetry backends.
Structured metadata may combine safe aggregate measurements with arbitrary content-bearing values.
anti_goals: Do not disable all telemetry when only payload content requires suppression.
Do not remove safe event identity, timing, status, verdict, error, or aggregate measurement fields solely because payload logging is disabled.
Do not treat an entire extensible metadata object as safe merely because some of its current keys are numeric counters.
Do not change the meaning of the runtime consent flag or enable payload logging implicitly.
validation_ladder: Inspect the parent and patched serializers to confirm every identified direct payload field moved behind the runtime consent check.
Run unit cases with payload logging disabled and assert absence of request text, response text, tool arguments, prompts, policies, tool-call content, and rationale.
Run paired enabled-mode cases and assert intentionally supported payload fields remain available.
Verify non-sensitive event name, function name, verdict result, and error fields remain in disabled mode.
For mixed metadata, verify only the explicit aggregate allowlist survives disabled mode and arbitrary nested keys do not.
Exercise every backend-specific representation of the same logical event to detect sink-specific redaction bypasses.
stop_conditions: Stop and defer if no authoritative runtime setting defines whether payload content may be logged.
Stop if the sensitive-field inventory or backend inventory cannot be established from implementation and call sites.
Do not declare completion if any affected sink still receives a classified payload in disabled mode.
Do not broaden the allowlist when a metadata key's safety cannot be established.
Stop and require an unconditional-removal decision if a field is prohibited even when payload logging is enabled.

records.episode_title: Bound sensitive and attacker-controlled data at diagnostic boundaries
atomic_titles: Sanitize and bound untrusted diagnostic text
Replace sensitive remote error bodies with bounded metadata
Verify diagnostic non-disclosure and structural safety
workflow_titles: Harden diagnostics that may contain sensitive or attacker-controlled data
when_to_use: An HTTP, messaging, gateway, persistence, or handler failure can place remote payloads or exception text into logs or caller-visible errors.
A credential-bearing request currently includes its remote error body in diagnostics.
User-controlled or server-controlled text can contain line breaks, terminal controls, invisible separators, bidi controls, or unbounded content.
anti_goals: Do not remove stable status codes or ordinary readable context needed to diagnose the failure.
Do not treat simple truncation as sufficient protection against control-character or line-forging attacks.
Do not log credential-adjacent response bodies merely because they may contain a useful server error message.
Do not change transport behavior, retry policy, or unrelated state-persistence semantics as part of the redaction contract.
validation_ladder: Diff review: enumerate each scoped dynamic diagnostic interpolation and classify it as omitted or sanitized and bounded.
Focused unit oracle: supply a recognizable remote error body and require exact status-only output.
Adversarial text oracle: inject newline, NUL, tab, ANSI, C1, Unicode separator, and bidi-control characters and assert diagnostic structure is unchanged.
Utility-preservation oracle: confirm stable status codes and ordinary readable error fragments remain available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the data provenance or disclosure policy cannot establish whether a payload must be omitted or may be sanitized and retained.
Stop if no diagnostic sink or propagated-error call site can be established from implementation evidence.
Do not claim completion if tests only check truncation and do not assert absence of sensitive sentinels or structural control characters.
Defer broader coverage claims when changed call sites lack direct adversarial tests.

records.episode_title: Add a transactional SQLite session backend with schema-backed summaries and bounded context reconstruction
atomic_titles: Move persistent session queries behind the storage contract
Persist canonical events and derived state in one transaction
Initialize persistent storage through recorded migrations
Make compaction entries self-contained for recent context
workflow_titles: Introduce a relational session backend without breaking session semantics
when_to_use: A new durable backend must implement an existing in-memory or file-backed event-session abstraction.
Resume, listing, statistics, or branch reconstruction requires indexed or materialized state instead of repeatedly scanning the full history.
One logical append updates canonical history and multiple derived representations that must not diverge.
anti_goals: Do not replace the append-only session event model with only a mutable snapshot.
Do not make backend-specific database concepts part of the reusable Session caller API.
Do not silently discard legacy compaction records that lack embedded retained messages.
Do not treat materialized summaries as independently writable sources of truth.
validation_ladder: Validate the migration ledger, required tables, active-leaf column, and indexes on a fresh database.
Run common storage behavior checks for metadata, names, aggregate statistics, labels, entry retrieval, and bounded paths.
Exercise create, list, open, append, navigation, fork, paging, and reopen through the relational repository.
Inspect persisted active-leaf, branch-membership, summary, and entry-materialization rows after representative operations.
Inject append and repository failures to verify transaction rollback, process-local state restoration, and database cleanup.
Verify retained-tail and legacy compaction context reconstruction produce the expected message ordering.
Verify the concrete database adapter binds both positional and named parameters.
stop_conditions: Stop if the parent and implementation states cannot establish a stable session behavior contract.
Stop if canonical entries and projections cannot be committed within one atomic persistence boundary.
Stop if reopen or failure-injection tests expose divergence among history, active leaf, branch membership, and summaries.
Defer promotion if only schema creation is tested without behavioral round trips and rollback checks.

records.episode_title: Keep session state available under SQLite contention and reconcile incomplete transcript migration
atomic_titles: Make session-row creation safe to repeat
Repair a missing session parent before appending messages
Keep persistence available after transient initialization failure
Give concurrent writers a bounded recovery window
Release the database lock between search context queries
Restore history from the most complete transcript source
workflow_titles: Recover session persistence after transient database contention
Prevent transcript truncation while two persistent stores coexist
when_to_use: Multiple processes or threads share an embedded session database and startup or flush operations can overlap.
A failed initial parent-row insert currently disables later persistence or leaves child-message writes unable to satisfy their parent relationship.
Search enrichment performs multiple database round trips while sharing the same connection lock.
anti_goals: Do not remove foreign-key enforcement or append orphaned messages.
Do not overwrite established session metadata during recovery.
Do not retry forever or conceal persistent storage failures.
Do not change message ordering or the existing flush cursor semantics.
validation_ladder: Statically verify finite timeout configuration, first-write-wins insertion, retained database lifecycle, pre-append parent repair, and reduced search lock scope.
Run unit tests for duplicate parent creation, missing-parent repair, no-overwrite behavior, post-repair child append, and timeout configuration.
Exercise a real two-writer workload to confirm transient contention clears without permanent feature loss; this integration check was not present in the inspected change.
stop_conditions: Stop if the database handle cannot be safely reused after the reported exception.
Stop if idempotent insertion would hide conflicting identifiers that must be rejected by the domain.
Stop if parent repair cannot preserve existing authoritative metadata.
Stop and investigate if contention consistently exceeds the bounded wait, indicating a persistent transaction or deadlock rather than a transient collision.

records.episode_title: Consolidate dynamic-tool persistence onto rollout session metadata while retaining schema compatibility
atomic_titles: Restore immutable session configuration from its authoritative history record
Remove writes, reads, and synchronization for the redundant state replica
Retain the unused persisted schema for mixed-version compatibility
Verify restoration through the real resume request boundary
workflow_titles: Consolidate duplicated persistent state without breaking restoration or older schemas
when_to_use: The same immutable or thread-start state is persisted in both an authoritative event/history record and a secondary database representation.
Resume or fork behavior can reconstruct the state from the authoritative record.
The duplicated path spans reads, writes, ingestion/backfill, reconciliation, or metadata synchronization and creates competing ownership.
A legacy schema may still be referenced by older supported binaries.
anti_goals: Do not change the dynamic-tool contract, ordering, description, input schema, namespace semantics, or caller override precedence.
Do not remove unrelated thread metadata persistence or backfill responsibilities.
Do not drop a legacy table merely because the current runtime stops using it.
Do not treat the secondary database as the new source of truth when the durable session record already owns the state.
validation_ladder: Static inspection: verify the runtime restoration branch reads the authoritative history record and preserves explicit-input precedence.
Call-site inspection: verify field-specific secondary-store APIs, ingestion, backfill, reconciliation, and metadata-patch propagation are absent.
Component validation: run the state, rollout, and thread-store package tests reported by the commit.
Behavioral integration: create and resume a thread with the secondary database enabled, then inspect the first resumed request for the complete restored field contract.
Compatibility validation: confirm legacy schema migrations remain; execute mixed-version database tests if such a harness is available.
stop_conditions: Stop if the authoritative record does not contain the field for all supported resume or fork cases.
Stop if any runtime consumer still depends exclusively on the secondary representation.
Stop before dropping the legacy schema unless supported-version policy and migration tests explicitly authorize it.
Stop if the integration test cannot distinguish restoration from explicit resupply or fixture defaults.
Stop if removing the field-specific plumbing also removes unrelated metadata persistence behavior.

records.episode_title: Serialize policy persistence and validate stored regular-expression rules
atomic_titles: Serialize persistent read-modify-write updates
Give each atomic write an exclusive staging file
Reject unsafe regular expressions at every state-ingress boundary
workflow_titles: Make file-backed policy updates race-safe and safe to restore
when_to_use: An event-driven component performs read-modify-write updates against one persistent structured-state file.
Concurrent or closely spaced updates can read the same prior snapshot or share a temporary pathname.
Persisted fields are later compiled or interpreted as executable matching expressions.
anti_goals: Do not change policy precedence, decisions, or the representation of accepted rule fields.
Do not serialize unrelated in-memory operations that do not request persistence.
Do not treat the heuristic regex check as a complete regular-expression complexity proof or silently rewrite rejected patterns.
validation_ladder: Unit-test the expression predicate with valid, malformed, overlong, and nested-quantifier examples.
Test the live update boundary to prove a rejected expression cannot mutate active state.
Test serialization content and the exclusive staging-file/open/write/rename protocol.
Add a concurrent persistent-update test that controls read/write timing and proves the final file contains every accepted update.
Load the resulting file and verify all accepted rules reconstruct successfully while unsafe stored rules are reported and omitted.
stop_conditions: Stop if the updater cannot identify one stable state target or cannot scope a serialization owner around all same-process writers.
Stop if expression-bearing inputs cannot be identified before compilation or persistence.
Do not claim multi-process lost-update prevention from unique staging files alone; the queue is local to one updater instance.
Do not claim the race is regression-tested until a test actually overlaps at least two persistence operations.
